questions.question: Broken suspension parts:
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports your vehicle and keeps the axles in place. Broken suspension parts are very dangerous.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Back up quickly to get out of other drivers' ways.
Try not to use the mirrors.

questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. When you can, use a helper to watch your blind spots.

questions.question: A skid caused by speeding up too fast can usually be stopped by:

options.text: Taking your foot off the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking your foot off the accelerator.
questions.explanation: To stop a skid caused by speeding up too fast, take your foot off the accelerator. This type of skid happens most often on snow or ice.

questions.question: When driving downhill, your vehicle will:

options.text: Travel at the same speed as on flat ground.

questions.explanation: Gravity makes your vehicle go faster when going downhill. Slow down before you start going downhill.

questions.question: Driving at night is:

options.text: Safer than driving during the day.
Just as safe as driving during the day.
More dangerous than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Driving at night is more dangerous than driving during the day because it is harder to see hazards in the dark.

questions.question: When putting out an electrical fire, you should:
questions.explanation: B:C fire extinguishers work on electrical fires and burning liquids. Do not use water on an electrical fire.

questions.question: If your vehicle is on fire and you don't know how to put it out, you should:

options.text: Try to spray the flames with water.
Move away from the flames and wait for firefighters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move away from the flames and wait for firefighters.
questions.explanation: If you don't know how to put out a fire, do not try. Move away from the flames and let firefighters handle it.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Speed up and slow down often.
Change your driving to match the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your driving to match the weather.
questions.explanation: On a slippery road, adjust your speed to fit the conditions. Your vehicle will take longer to stop, so increase your distance from other vehicles. Avoid speeding up and slowing down often.

questions.question: When are people usually the least alert?
questions.explanation: Most drivers are least alert at night, especially after midnight. Tired driving crashes happen more often at night.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:

options.text: Pull out the air brake knob.

questions.explanation: To make a normal stop in a vehicle with air brakes, press the brake pedal down.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination, which trailer should be directly behind the cab?
questions.explanation: The heaviest trailer should be closest to the tractor. The lightest trailer should be at the rear.

questions.question: A slack adjuster should move no more than ____ from the push rod.
questions.explanation: Before driving, check each slack adjuster. Pull it to make sure it moves no more than one inch from the push rod. If it moves more than one inch, it needs repair.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?
questions.explanation: ABS helps you maintain control during hard braking. It does not necessarily shorten stopping distance.

questions.question: How many air lines does a combination vehicle have?
questions.explanation: A combination vehicle has two air lines: the service line and the emergency line.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, what happens to stopping distance?

options.text: It is longer than on a regular driving surface.
It is not as long as on a regular driving surface.
It is about the same as on a regular driving surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is longer than on a regular driving surface.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on slippery surfaces because there is less traction.

questions.question: When operating a vehicle with a dual air brake system, what should the driver do before driving?

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up to ensure fuel reaches the engine.
Let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
Begin driving just after the vehicle starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving, allow the air compressor to build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems. Check the air pressure gauges.

questions.question: Why is watching the road ahead important?

options.text: It gives you time to plan how to avoid hazards.
It is not encouraged because it distracts you.
It is only important in heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to plan how to avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: Always watch for hazards ahead. This gives you time to react before you reach them.

questions.question: What is the leading cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is the leading cause of injury and death in work zones. Slow down when driving through work zones.

questions.question: How can you stop a skid caused by acceleration?

options.text: Remove your foot from the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove your foot from the accelerator.
questions.explanation: Acceleration skids happen on slippery surfaces. Remove your foot from the accelerator to stop the skid.

questions.question: When visibility is poor and you are near other drivers, which lights should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when visibility is poor and you are near other drivers. High beams can make it harder for other drivers to see.
